divergences.en_says: founded by Herzl in 1897; earlier Proto-Zionism via Hovevei Zion
divergences.other_says: history begins earlier and is linked to Judaism and Jewish history (AR); appeared 19th century from multi-millennial religious heritage centered on Zion (FR)
divergences.evidence_en: Zionism, as an organised nationalist movement, is generally considered to have been founded by Theodor Herzl in 1897

divergences.other_says: redefinition of Jewish identity amid emancipation, European nationalism and rise of antisemitism (FR)
divergences.evidence_other: dans un contexte marqué par l’émancipation, le nationalisme européen et la montée de l’antisémitisme

divergences.other_says: importance diminished since 1948 but movement continues; 40% of world Jews now live in Israel; unique historical case of nation re-established after diaspora (AR)
debates on place of Jewish religion in Zionism and on location/borders of the Jewish state (CA)
takes form through secular, religious or socialist currents (FR)
divergences.evidence_other: à travers divers courants — laïques, religieux ou socialistes

summary: EN emphasizes Herzl, the 1897 congress and the secular Jewish-majority state in Mandatory Palestine. AR adds pre-modern Jewish historical links and post-1948 continuity/success metrics. FR highlights European nationalist context, antisemitism and multiple ideological currents. CA frames the topic around institutional construction, demographic debates and internal divisions over religion and borders. These create distinct introductory emphases rather than direct factual contradictions.
